headline: High-risk shared-server workflow: Langflow can write and egress broadly while social-auto-upload can push account data to external platforms, creating dangerous default-path leakage and action cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and chain tools in graph flows, while social-auto-upload consumes local files and account data in CLI/headless mode. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could let attacker-controlled content in one agent influence the other, though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or file bundle
IF Langflow flow nodes ingest uploaded file contents as instructions
IF social-auto-upload parses generated text from Langflow without sanitization
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated text as instructions
Add a manual review step before passing artifacts between agents
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials, and it has broad network egress. social-auto-upload touches account data and media files and also has broad egress to external services. If they share a workspace or account artifacts, sensitive inputs can flow from Langflow into social-media uploads or external APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Langflow stores secrets or user inputs in files accessible to social-auto-upload
IF social-auto-upload uploads media or account data derived from Langflow outputs
IF both agents run under the same OS account or shared volume
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict outbound network destinations for each agent
Review uploaded artifacts before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the filesystem, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; social-auto-upload is CLI-based and may also manipulate local files and external APIs, though it cannot write the filesystem per profile. The overlap on shared mutable resources is enough for conflicts if they operate on the same workspace, but the profile does not show unrestricted write on both sides, so high is not justified.
conditions: IF both agents target the same output directory
IF Langflow flows and social-auto-upload run concurrently
IF either agent assumes exclusive ownership of generated media or account files
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run each agent under a separate account
Make shared artifacts immutable after creation
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and produce intermediate outputs that may be treated as authoritative, while social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader to external platforms. If Langflow-generated content is fed into the uploader without verification, errors or hallucinations can become irreversible public posts. This is a default-dangerous cascade because the second agent can act on the first agent's output.
conditions: IF Langflow output is passed directly into social-auto-upload
IF no human approval gate exists before upload
IF the uploader posts to public accounts or channels
mitigations: Require manual approval before upload
Validate titles, captions, and media against source files
Add a diff/checklist step for generated content
Limit uploads to a staging account
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media for public-platform posting. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a precise mismatch cannot be proven; however, the combination creates a plausible retention and account-data compliance gap if regulated or personal data is routed through the pair. The uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into Langflow flows
IF social-auto-upload retains account or media artifacts beyond policy
IF the deployment requires specific residency or retention controls
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Document retention for flow outputs and uploaded media
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Use separate storage buckets with explicit retention settings
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls
